name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: MAVAZI | 18th Annual Taste of Africa
description:
MAVAZI, meaning “clothing” in Swahili, is the 2026 edition of the African Student Association’s annual Taste of Africa showcase at The George Washington University. This year’s theme highlights the power of fashion as a form of cultural expression, storytelling, and identity across the African continent and diaspora.

Through a dynamic runway experience, MAVAZI brings together traditional and contemporary African fashion, showcasing the richness of textiles, beadwork, craftsmanship, and design. Each piece tells a story—reflecting history, heritage, and the evolving creativity of African designers and communities.

More than just a fashion show, MAVAZI is a celebration of culture, artistry, and unity. The event will feature curated looks, live performances, and an immersive atmosphere that honors the diversity and vibrancy of African cultures. Attendees can expect an evening that blends fashion, music, and storytelling into a powerful and memorable experience.

Each year, TEDxFoggyBottom is brought to life by over 50 undergraduate students at The George Washington University in Washington, DC, who work to bring together some of the world's most incredible innovators, thinkers, and doers to inspire and collaborate with the Foggy Bottom community. name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
location: USC Presentation Space (Across from Chaat House)
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

description:
Join us for a gala celebrating the Asian American diaspora in the 2000’s through culture, community, dinner, speakers, performances, activities, and DANCING!!! ✨💝


⭐️Theme Details:

The 2000s embodied vibrancy, color, and a global explosion of expression that shaped our visual identity, cultural style, and the nostalgia we carry today. It marked a pivotal era in the emergence of “Asian American” as a widely recognized and evolving identity. Our connection to the 2000s is deepened by our growing voice in pop culture and by the fact that these were the years our parents spent raising us. 🫂💕 Yet in honoring these histories, GWU AASA takes on the responsibility of maintaining a critical lens. The same violence that underlaid the U.S. in the 2000s informs the escalations we witness two decades later. As we celebrate the struggles and resilience of Asian migrants and earlier generations of Asian Americans, we must not allow commodified nostalgia to obscure those violent processes. We remain committed—always—to our political line. 🫂💓✨

If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

location: USC Presentation Space (Across from Chaat House)
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

name: "The Right Track" Film Screening and Panel Discussion
description:
The George Washington University Office of Advocacy and Support (OAS) and Rights4Girls invite you to a film screening of the groundbreaking documentary "The Right Track" onTuesday, March 31st, from 6:30pm-9:00pm in the Continental Ballroom of the University Student Center at located at 800 21st St NW, Washington, D.C.

 

Through the eyes of those who live it, "The Right Track" documentary spotlights the fight to end sex trafficking and human exploitation across North America. At its heart is the Survivor Model—a transformative approach that decriminalizes prostituted individuals while imposing strict penalties on pimps, traffickers, and sex buyers. Discover the courage it takes to escape “the life” on and off the track and the momentum needed to end sex trafficking for good. The Right Track is a must-watch for anyone invested in human dignity and justice. Click here to watch the trailer. 

 

After the film screening, please join us for a panel moderated by Carolina Bazan, Senior Program Manager at Rights4Girls. We will be joined by three incredible panelists: Peter Qualliotine, Melanie Thompson, and Cristian Eduardo. Click here to learn more about our panelists. 

 

GW's Office of Advocacy and Support (OAS) is a university office that provides trauma-informed and healing-centered confidential support to student survivors of intimate partner violence, sexual assault, and stalking. Click here to learn more about OAS.  

 

Rights4Girls advocates for the dignity and rights of young women and girls so that every girl can be safe and live a life free of violence and exploitation. Click here to learn more about Rights4Girls.

In alignment with the Strategic Framework, and inspired by principles of community - derived from scholars, researchers, activists, changemakers, youth, and organizers - the 10th Diversity Summit will be named OneGW Summit: Community, Culture & Inclusion. With deep intention and purpose, we believe that centering the GW community in our work to amplify and celebrate diversity, collectively foster inclusion, and strive toward equity for all is how we move forward, together, as OneGW.

Remaining committed to our longstanding values, the OneGW Summit: Community, Culture & Inclusion will continue to be grounded in learning, dialogue, research, storytelling, and education on identity, social issues, diverse viewpoints, and sustainable positive action. The Summit will be:

A time of reflection, ideation, collaboration, and inspiration
An opportunity and curated experience for the whole GW community to bring all of their identities, lived experiences, stories, and various perspectives into a shared space
A groundswelling of engagement through civil discourse, deep listening, and healthy debate

It is our hope that the Summit is affirming to all and across all identities and viewpoints.

From celebrating milestones that helped us reach 10 years, to honoring members of the GW community making a significant impact in the world, and more, the Summit will serve as a catalyst for deeper engagement, connection, and meaningful dialogue across all differences. The Summit will honor the coexistence of multiple truths, demonstrating our strength to come together, break bread, and build as OneGW.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: CAPS Presents: Healing with Clay and Paint, Understanding & Managing Anxiety
description:
We often intellectualize the anxious thoughts we experience. Those thoughts overwhelm us and we feel out of control. Research shows that our nervous systems and minds can quickly regulate when we connect with stable, earthy, and sensory experiences. Moreover, doing this repeatedly and making it a practice can even help in understanding, accepting, and finding a place for the overwhelming thoughts and experiences in our lives. So, let’s literally get out of our heads.

Join us to learn how to connect and regulate your body to better understand and address your anxiety. Week over week we will use two tactile forms of art to help you explore your internal narratives and increase emotional awareness. The group will begin with a grounding exercise, followed by a guided activity using either mediums or both, followed by a short group reflection before closing.

P.s. You need no artistic skill to engage with clay and paint, so please do not let that be a deterrent from joining us.

While DC suffers from significant light pollution, the Unistellar telescope's unique software reduces the impact of the city lights on images of the night sky in real time, giving us a great view (weather permitting!) of planets, galaxies, nebulae and star clusters. On Tuesday, March 17 starting at 8:30pm, we will be observing various solar-system and deep sky objects such as Jupiter, the Orion Nebula and the Pleiades. Download the Unistellar app on your smartphone or tablet to follow along with our observations on your personal device. Feel free to drop by to observe for just a few minutes or stay for a while!

name: 46th Patricia Roberts Harris Banquet
description:
The George Washington University Law School BLSA invites you to attend the 46th Annual Patricia Roberts Harris Awards Banquet.

The George Washington University Law School Black Law Students Association (BLSA) is pleased to announce the 46th Annual Patricia Roberts Harris Awards Banquet, which will be held on March 28th, 2026, at the JW Marriott in Washington, D.C. Mrs. Harris, a distinguished alumna of The George Washington University National Law Center (now The George Washington University Law School), achieved remarkable milestones in her career. After graduating at the top of her class in 1960, she became a dedicated public servant, earning numerous accolades and pioneering many firsts. Among her many achievements, she was the first African-American woman to serve as a United States Ambassador, a member of the United States Cabinet, and as Dean of an American law school (Howard University School of Law).


In the spirit of her incredible achievements, this banquet serves as an occasion to honor and recognize BLSA’s outstanding graduating students, alumni, and sponsors, as well as the law school’s dedicated faculty and staff. Building strong, enduring relationships with legal organizations across the District of Columbia is central to ensuring that students have opportunities to follow in Mrs. Harris’ path. Therefore, BLSA extends an invitation for you to join us in this celebration of our distinguished alumna and exceptional community.
